description.narrative:
The Palestinian Medical Relief Society (PMRS) and subsidiary MRS is a one of the largest health NGOs in the OPT and a leading grassroot community-based health organisation that works in more than 500 localities across the OPT. It is also one of the leading organisations working on youth friendly health services and one stop centres across the OPT. Under this project, PRMS and subsidiary MRS will be responsible of the overall implementation of the action in West Bank and EJ, including upgrading the OSCs in Hebron and Beit Hanina (EJ), provide multisectoral GBV-SRH services, deploy mobile outreach teams, promote the Mostashari app to reach to the most marginalised adolescents and youth to link them to the OSCs, and develop referral protocols in the WB and EJ.
PMRS will equip and rehabilitate two OSCs, each tailored to the specific needs and contexts of the target locations. In the West Bank, PMRS will invest inenhancing their health OSC in Hebron, while in East Jerusalem MRS will transform their youth hub into a centre that provides education and training on GBV-SRHR. These improvements will ensure that the three OSCs have improved infrastructural and technical capacities to actively provide equitable and accessible multi-sectoral GBV and SRHR information and services. These services encompass a wide range of vital areas, including health, mental health, psychosocial support, legal assistance, and referral to shelter services. These OSCs will also continue to offer youth-friendly services, serving as information points for SRH and family planning, preconception, ante and post-natal care, laboratory services, access to doctors and pharmaceutical services. To create safe and protected spaces for youth to access GBV-SRHR information and develop awareness and skills for informed life choices regarding SRHR-GBV prevention, the youth safe spaces, in Hebron OSCs, will undergo rehabilitation and customization. In EJ, MRS will invest in their centre located in Beit Hanina, previously functioning as a clinic. The OSC will collaborate with MRS’s comprehensive mobile clinics and outreach teams to ensure integrated services that align with the OSC objectives, connecting youth to the centre. MRS will establish a dedicated youth-friendly health service room at the OSC, specifically designed to provide GBV-SRH services. PMRS will promote the Mostashari app, a specialized platform offering comprehensive SRH services, information, and interaction with qualified youth health professionals. Additionally, PMRS helplines will provide remote GBV-SRH counselling and referral across the OPT. PMRS will work to promotethe collective work and the adoption of established referral protocols by existing networks and service providers in the OSCs. Thiswill be achieved by developing and updating GBV-SRH referral protocols in the OSCs, aligning them with standard operating procedures (SOPs) of case managemen in EJ, as well as with the national referral system in the West Bank. Additionally, youth-friendly maps will be developed, illustrating referral pathways, and disseminated through public/digital spaces, the Mostashari app and social media. Based on the established referral protocols, a capacity building program will be designed to train service providers on the utilization of GBV-SRH referral protocols, as well as delivering youth-friendly and gender-sensitive GBV-SRH services. PMRS will seeks toinfluence public opinion on GBV-SRH priorities and increase youth/adolescent leadership by strengthening the storytelling capacity of young men and women, focusing on GBV and SRHR topics, while also supporting youth-led initiatives, such as awareness-raising campaigns, community engagement initiatives and peer support networks.

participating-org.narrative:
PMRS is a grassroots, community-based Palestinian health organization. PMRS was founded in 1979 by a group of Palestinian doctors and health professionals seeking to supplement the decayed and inadequate health infrastructure caused by years of Israeli military occupation. It is non-profit, voluntary, and one of the largest health NGOs in Palestine. PMRS national health programs emphasize prevention, education, community participation, and the empowerment of people.
Since its inception, PMRS has grownfrom a small nucleusof volunteer health workers responding to the increasing healthcare needs in underserved areas, to a leading Palestinian health non-governmental organization (NGO). PMRS now extends its services to over 1.4 million Palestinians in theWest Bank and Gaza Strip, providing improved models of healthcare that are built on sound scientific bases and specifically adapted to the Palestinian context. In the years prior to the Intifada, PMRS made a significant contribution to the creation of aPalestinian national health infrastructure, replacing the fragmented health system inherited from years of Israeli occupation.
PMRS role in health service provision, alongside the Palestinian Ministry of Health (MOH), United Nations Relief and Work Agency (UNRWA) and other health NGOs, has steadily progressed. In light of this, PMRS has established strong links with the public health sector, leading to the creation of a subcontracting system between the MOH and PMRS and other NGOs, such that the MOH canmake use of their health services.
In addition, PMRS has developed its strategy to build model health programs, such as the Womens Health Program, Child Health Program, School Health Program, and Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR) Program. Based on its considerable experience in service provision; awareness of the needs and characteristics of local communities; professional expertise; and field worker commitment, PMRS develops models and protocolsthat can be tested in the field, and disseminated topublic and NGO sector institutions – at both local and regional level.
At the same time PMRS is highly involved in policy making at national level, to influence the adoption of legislation that supports civil society and the creation of a modern democratic state. PMRS works on this with other Palestinian NGOs through the Palestinian NGO network (PNGO) and other joint forums that link between the public and NGO sectors.
PMRS in Gaza employs about 100 people spread between the headquarters in Gaza City, its four clinics, one non communicable diseases (NCD) centre and two rehabilitation centers. The organization also runs two mobile clinics which provide emergency primary health care to communities in marginalized and/or isolatedareas. It also conducts awareness activities on various health, hygiene and social issues affecting peoples quality of life. PMRSrelies on its network of around 150 volunteers to reach out to all levels of society all over the Strip. First aid teams have beenactivated to face the emergency and save lives. Moreover, PMRS has agreements with the Gaza Ministry of Health according to which the former refers patients in need of secondary health care to the latter hospitals.
